standard_prerequisites.name: Existence of a system of parameters extending a given element avoiding the minimal primes
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the element g used in the perturbation argument.

standard_prerequisites.name: In a Noetherian ring a power of the radical of an ideal lies in the ideal
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the exponent n from which N = n + 1 is built.

standard_prerequisites.name: The relation 1 + a is a unit when a lies in the maximal ideal
standard_prerequisites.use: Is what makes the first generator absorb the perturbation without changing the ideal.

core_obligations: Use the system-of-parameters existence lemma to find g in m such that f, g is a system of parameters for R, so that m = sqrt((f, g)) (proof lines 38122-38124).
By the Noetherian power lemma choose n with m^n contained in (f, g), and claim that N = n + 1 works (proof lines 38124-38127).
For h in m^N use the choice of N to write h = a f + b g with a and b in m (proof lines 38128-38129).
Compute the displayed chain (f + h, g) = (f + a f + b g, g) = ((1 + a) f, g) = (f, g), using that 1 + a is a unit of R (proof lines 38130-38132).
Conclude both that f + h, g is a system of parameters and that the two lengths agree (proof lines 38133-38134).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian local ring (R, m) of dimension two and an element f in m contained in no minimal prime of R, and asserts the existence of g in m and an integer N such that f and g form a system of parameters and such that for every h in m^N, the pair f + h and g again forms a system of parameters with length_R(R/(f, g)) = length_R(R/(f + h, g)) (source lines 38107-38119). The proof is an explicit computation parallel to the higher-dimensional statement. By the system-of-parameters existence lemma there is g in m making f, g a system of parameters, so that m = sqrt((f, g)); the Noetherian power lemma then gives n with m^n contained in (f, g), and the proof claims N = n + 1 works (proof lines 38122-38127). The verification is a direct ideal computation: for h in m^N one writes h = a f + b g with a and b in m, and the displayed chain (f + h, g) = (f + a f + b g, g) = ((1 + a) f, g) = (f, g) follows because 1 + a is a unit of R, which gives both the system-of-parameters claim and the equality of lengths (proof lines 38128-38134). The non-routine content is the choice N = n + 1 that lets the perturbation be absorbed into the first generator.
